text:
eli: Hey team — multiple customers (C-2124, C-2125) reporting 502/504s on the hosted inference API since ~13:02 UTC. Support queue is lighting up. Any oncall?
ops-bot: deploy event: rollout/route_selector_v2 started at 13:01 UTC, initial weight 30% (triggered by devon, PR #789) :information_source:
devon: I flipped route_selector_v2 for a weighted slice (30%) to route traffic to the new routing logic. Thought it was a safe canary.
maya: oncall SRE — I see a spike at 13:03. Error rate ~7.8% in us-west-2, traces show gateway errors when proxying to inference-backend instances (inference-srv-2).
sanjay: runtime team here — any config changes beyond route_selector_v2?
devon: not that I recall. Just the selector flag.
eli: repro from customer:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <long-jwt>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"input": "hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":"upstream read: connection reset by peer"}
eli: they said the same requests succeed if retried after a few seconds.
maya: grabbing edge logs... seeing a pattern: requests routed to slice B (new selector) have truncated Authorization headers — looks like header cut at ~128 chars. Backends reject and the proxy reports upstream reset.
sanjay: that matches a recent sidecar change (PR #800) for the new slice that enforces header size limit for certain internal headers. It may be too aggressive for JWTs used by hosted customers.
anna: (product) slice B was meant for internal dedicated customers; we missed scoping to avoid hosted traffic.
devon: ack. That was my mistake on rollout targeting. Rolling back now to 0% for route_selector_v2.
deploy-bot: rollback job created for rollout/route_selector_v2, progressing to 0% target (started 13:18 UTC).
maya: mitigation while rollback runs: enabling header passthrough on the edge for affected slice id. Patch command:
```bash
kubectl -n edge patch config edge-config --type merge -p '{"spec":{"preserveHeaders":["Authorization"]}}'
```
maya: applied, routing test shows Authorization preserved on new requests to slice B.
eli: I informed ACME support: we have a rollback + header passthrough; providing ETA ~10min. Customer acknowledged, asked about billing impact.
devon: rollback completed at 13:25 UTC, rollout weight back to 0%.
deploy-bot: rollback finished — all replicas back to previous routing. Health checks: passing.
maya: monitoring: error rate dropped to baseline within ~3 minutes after rollback/patch. Traces confirm requests are no longer hitting the sidecar that trimmed headers.
sanjay: root cause summary: the new routing sidecar enforces a header-size policy that truncated long Authorization JWTs. That caused auth failures which surfaced as upstream closures/502s at the gateway. The selector was unintentionally applied to hosted traffic due to mis-scoped rollout targeting.
anna: actions: 1) dev to add gating to prevent header-truncation policy in hosted path, 2) release to tighten rollout scoping, 3) support to confirm with affected customers and issue RCA.
devon: I'll open PRs: add an automated check that rejects rollouts touching routes with external auth headers and add a quick rollback runbook step.
maya: I'll add an alert for unexpected header-size rejections and extend canary telemetry to include header-preservation checks.
eli: Closing loop with customers and noting credit for retries. I'll file tickets C-2124/C-2125 with the mitigation timeline.
eli: Thanks everyone — posting for postmortem scheduling. :thumbsup:
